title: Distribution, Dev Experience, Cutover, And Cleanup
objective: Finish the Bun-based distribution path, complete local development ergonomics, flip the product to Server V2 by default, and remove legacy architecture once the new server is credible.

steps.name: Finalize the composite local dev command graph
steps.description: Wire the server runtime watcher, OpenAPI watcher, SDK watcher, and app dev server together behind one practical local command so contributors can iterate without manual restarts.
successFactors: One dev command starts the intended local graph.
The command matches the watch model in `local-dev.md`.
Developers can edit routes, schemas, SDK helpers, and app code without hand-sync work.

steps.name: Harden OpenAPI and SDK watcher behavior
steps.description: Make sure regeneration is debounced, deterministic, and isolated enough that spec or SDK writes do not cause needless server restarts or watch loops.
successFactors: Generated-file changes do not trigger backend restart loops.
Regeneration only writes changed output.
Developers can leave the watch graph running continuously.

steps.name: Finalize source-consumption SDK dev behavior
steps.description: Ensure the app can consume the SDK package source or generated output directly in dev without slow rebuild-to-dist cycles unless packaging explicitly requires them.
successFactors: The app sees SDK changes immediately in local dev.
TypeScript and Vite pick up changes without extra packaging steps.
Any required build step is reserved for packaging, not normal iteration.

steps.name: Implement the Bun compile build for Server V2
steps.description: Create the build pipeline that compiles `apps/server-v2` into the per-platform standalone executable format described in `distribution.md`.
successFactors: A Bun-compiled Server V2 executable can be produced for the supported targets.
The build process is scriptable and repeatable.
Build-time metadata and manifests can be injected cleanly.

steps.name: Embed sidecars and runtime manifest
steps.description: Package `opencode`, `opencode-router`, and the runtime manifest into the compiled Server V2 executable using the chosen Bun embedding approach.
successFactors: The compiled server carries the expected sidecar payloads and manifest.
The embedding approach is deterministic and inspectable.
The packaging matches the model described in `distribution.md`.

steps.name: Implement first-run extraction
steps.description: Extract embedded sidecars into a persistent versioned runtime directory on first run and reuse them on later runs instead of re-extracting into temp-like paths.
successFactors: Runtime extraction uses a persistent versioned directory.
Executable bits or platform-specific launch requirements are handled.
Repeated runs reuse existing verified assets.

steps.name: Add extraction locking and atomic replace behavior
steps.description: Prevent concurrent startup races and partial extraction corruption by implementing locking, atomic replacement, and interrupted-extraction handling.
successFactors: Concurrent launches do not corrupt the runtime directory.
Interrupted extraction can recover safely.
Runtime startup behavior remains predictable under race conditions.

steps.name: Implement runtime cleanup or garbage collection rules
steps.description: Define and implement how old extracted runtime versions are cleaned up safely without deleting an in-use runtime.
successFactors: Old runtimes can be cleaned up deliberately.
The cleanup strategy does not break rollback or currently running versions.
The behavior is documented in code or operational notes.

steps.name: Validate macOS signing and notarization behavior
steps.description: Prototype or validate the codesigning and notarization behavior for the main server executable and extracted sidecars so the preferred packaging model is proven on macOS.
successFactors: There is a clear answer on whether extracted sidecars need separate signing treatment.
Gatekeeper or notarization behavior is understood well enough for release planning.
Any unresolved macOS packaging risk is recorded in `open-questions.md`.

steps.name: Implement the Windows signing path
steps.description: Add the CI or release automation needed to sign the Windows desktop artifact, the standalone server, and the Windows sidecars as described in `distribution.md`.
successFactors: Windows signing is an explicit release capability, not a future assumption.
The final server executable and embedded sidecars have a clear signing flow.
Required secrets and verification steps are documented.

steps.name: Validate Windows AV and SmartScreen behavior
steps.description: Test or prototype first-run extraction and child-process launch on Windows so sidecar extraction does not create avoidable trust or startup problems.
successFactors: Windows startup behavior is understood before broad rollout.
Stable runtime-directory extraction is validated against AV or SmartScreen concerns.
Any packaging adjustments needed for Windows are captured explicitly.

steps.name: Bundle Server V2 into the desktop app
steps.description: Ship the compiled Server V2 runtime with the desktop app and ensure desktop launch paths use that bundled runtime instead of the old multi-process local stack.
successFactors: Desktop builds include the matching Server V2 runtime.
The app launches only that bundled server for the default path.
Desktop no longer launches `opencode` or router directly in the target path.

steps.name: Flip the desktop default to Server V2
steps.description: Once the new path is credible, switch the desktop startup default so normal users boot into Server V2 instead of the legacy local runtime path.
successFactors: Normal desktop startup uses Server V2 by default.
A temporary escape hatch exists only if still needed for rollback.
The default path aligns with the thin-client/server-first architecture.

steps.name: Flip app default routing to Server V2
steps.description: Make Server V2 the default backend path for migrated app features and retain the legacy path only as a temporary fallback if absolutely necessary.
successFactors: Normal product traffic uses Server V2.
Legacy mode is no longer the primary path.
Any remaining fallback is clearly temporary and narrowly scoped.

steps.name: Remove rollout and migration scaffolding that is no longer needed
steps.description: Delete temporary rollout branches, legacy shims, feature flags, or normalization code once the migrated surfaces no longer need them.
successFactors: Migration scaffolding is removed instead of fossilizing.
The app and server codepaths become simpler after cutover.
Deletion happens only after the replacement path is verified.

steps.name: Delete legacy server codepaths
steps.description: Remove the old server implementation once all consumers have moved so Server V2 becomes the only meaningful server implementation in the repo.
successFactors: No active product path depends on the old server.
Legacy code deletion is explicit and verified.
The repo no longer implies a permanent dual-server architecture.

steps.name: Delete or archive obsolete orchestrator control-plane code
steps.description: Remove orchestrator behavior that only existed to provide a separate control plane or bootstrap layer once the server has absorbed those responsibilities.
successFactors: Orchestrator is no longer a separate product control plane.
Residual host-shell code is clearly justified if anything remains.
The codebase reflects the collapsed architecture described in the docs.

steps.name: Run the full automated validation suite
steps.description: Execute the full contract, server, SDK, app integration, and any packaging validation commands required to prove the new architecture is healthy before release or PR creation.
successFactors: All major automated checks are run and reported.
Contract drift, runtime behavior, and app integrations are all covered.
Any failing area is visible with exact commands and results.

steps.name: Run end-to-end product validation
steps.description: Validate the real product flow, including Docker or Chrome MCP based checks if available, and capture evidence such as screenshots or video for final review where relevant.
successFactors: The implemented flow is tested end to end, not only by unit or integration tests.
Evidence for the final working product path is captured when possible.
If some end-to-end step cannot run, the exact gap and reproduction commands are recorded.

steps.name: Publish the final cutover and release checklist
steps.description: Capture the final cutover state, release gates, known residual debt, and any manual reviewer or operator steps so Server V2 can stop being a planning concept and become the default runtime architecture.
successFactors: The final rollout state is documented clearly.
Remaining debt or manual steps are explicit rather than hidden.
Phase 10 ends with a shippable, supportable Server V2 runtime story.
